messages:
mira (PM): OK team — quick sync. First 30d after GA we need a clear rule: which bugs get immediate hotfixes vs. which go into the next mini-iteration. My proposal: p99 regressions, data-loss, and security = hotfix; all UX polish + nonblocking feature requests = next iteration. Thoughts?
alex (ENG): +1 on the triage buckets. Need to add anything that increases token cost for customers to hotfix list? we had one case yesterday where inference cost spiked.
rob (DS): agree on p99 and sec. For cost regressions can we be more specific? maybe ">20% unit cost delta" or customer-facing billing impact.
sofia (SRE): From ops POV, anything that affects availability (error rate, timeouts) should be hotfix by default. Also we should tag incidents as "postlaunch-critical" so oncall knows priority.
jen (PD): Customers A and C raised requests for small UX tweaks that are driving churn signals (qual feedback). They are nonblocking but high impact. Can we reserve 15% of the mini-iteration for high-impact customer asks?
mira (PM): That sounds reasonable. Proposal update: hotfix if one of {p99 latency regressions, availability, security, >20% unit cost increase, data-loss}. Otherwise: classify as "high-impact customer ask" (up to 15% capacity) or backlog.
alex (ENG): Sounds good. For enforcement: we need a simple triage checklist in the bug template so triage can label "hotfix-yes/no". I'll add a checklist PR.
rob (DS): Also recommend adding an automated cost-regression check from telemetry that raises a flag when token cost delta >20% across a rolling 6h window. I can prototype a grafana alert.
sofia (SRE): +1. And can we define an SLA for response time on hotfixes? e.g., triage within 1h, patch within 24h for critical, 3 business days for high but not critical.
mira (PM): Good call. Let's formalize: triage 1h, patch target 24h for critical; 72h for severity-2. We can put exact wording in the runbook.
jen (PD): For customer asks: we should require a short impact statement and a commit to measure success (1-2 metrics). That will help justify the 15% carveout.
alex (ENG): On rollout strategy: prefer canary for any change touching runtime or model weights. fallback policy should be automatic to previous model version if error rate >1% within the canary window.
canary-bot: Deploy started: canary/ga-hotfix-202703 -> 10% traffic. Monitoring hooks: latency, errors, token-cost.
sofia (SRE): If canary fails, page oncall and trigger rollback. We'll add a standardized failure set for automated rollback.
mira (PM): Action items: alex add triage checklist PR by EOD, rob prototype cost-alert by Thu, jen draft customer-ask template, sofia update runbook with SLA + rollback conditions. I'll consolidate into a short policy doc after you add items. Anyone object?
alex (ENG): No objections. I'll also add an example of the bug template with the cost section.
rob (DS): I'll link the alert to a dashboard and add a one-click runbook link.
jen (PD): Will prioritize two customer asks for the 15% slot and share success metrics.
sofia (SRE): I'll schedule a brief oncall training for the new tags and SLA.
mira (PM): Great — thanks. I'll post the policy draft in #product later and schedule a 20m sync tomorrow to finalize. :thumbsup:
